text: MLPs at tied optimizer/lr/T and low Δ: compare LayerNorm count, residual status and task-specific exceptions; do NOT score a residual path as exactly one extra LN. For multivariate MSE with both Δ<0.1, a plain net with one extra LN is favored (K1076: lab 23/31, MSE ratio 0.906). Older more-LN corpus counts: multivariate 61/72, univariate 57/69, tabular Δ<0.1 41/45; these are not factor-isolated effects. At equal LN, regression rectifiers are a preference (K1008), not a full ranking rule. Use K1074 for regression depth, K1039 for shared SGD, K1020/K1077 for spirals, K1061 for deep plain tails, K1018/K1065 for XOR, K1009/K1033 for tabular budget reversals.
mechanism: LayerNorm and skips can improve signal propagation, but observed pairwise rankings do not establish a fixed exchange rate between them. Task, activation, depth, optimizer and normalization placement interact.

regime.note: Tied optimizer/lr/T; low displacement; task-specific rules take precedence. Residual is not a full LN point.

phase: LN-count win rate: multivariate 61-11, univariate 57-12 (lab same-residual more-LN: multivariate at 32768 samples 8/9, ratio 0.38; univariate 37/39), tabular Δ<0.1 41-4 but Δ>=0.1 less-LN 17-6 (K1009); residual at equal LN is the weakest term (lab regression 19/29, ratio ~0.96; q_ca0dea plain beat its residual twin); spiral: K1020; XOR plain+LN vs residual 6/10.

text: Tabular CE, 1024 rows, 2-16 Gaussian features, SHARED optimizer/lr/T and Δ≥0.1: shallow, smooth and fewer-LN are separate empirical preferences, not an additive architecture score. Older corpus: shallow wins 21/26, fewer-LN 17/23, smooth 16/16; combined rule 26/32 arch-only winners. Do not discard a residual+LN advantage solely for smooth activation or width (q_11a5f0); width was not isolated. At Δ<0.1 older more-LN wins 41/45, deeper 35/52, but 32-epoch depth reversals can start near Δ0.03 (K1033). Epochs/data rule matter: see K1073 for optimizer sweet spots and K1056 for activation. These are conditional ranking observations, not proof that every Δ≥0.1 boundary is learned.
mechanism: Observed architecture preferences change with displacement and examples seen, but these rankings do not independently measure boundary fit or confidence calibration. Overconfidence is a competing explanation, not a condition proven solely by Delta.

regime.note: Shared optimizer/lr/T; no additive architecture score or factor-isolated width effect.

phase: Δ_shared<0.1: more LN 41-4, deeper 35-17; Δ_shared≥0.1: shallower 21-5, less-LN 17-6, smooth act 16/16 (counterexample q_87182b: more early LN in residual LeakyReLU won). Across Δ (mixed questions) prefer Δ≈0.1-0.3 over ≥3× larger (K1021).

text: XOR CE, 1024 rows, ≥8 features, shared Adam/AdamW/RMSprop lr/T and Δ≥0.05: favor smooth activations (lab 15/16, CE ratio 0.78; corpus 6/6). Do not apply a universal shallow/fewer-LN score. More-LN wins only 8/32 lab but 5/11 corpus; fewer-LN is a preference. Depth depends on residuals (K1065): only the ≥3-block gap favors a ≤2-block net (lab 5/5, ratio 0.51; corpus 2/3). Below Δ0.05, more LN wins 33/41 (ratio 0.93), activation is mixed (smooth 3/8), and depth is conditional. With <8 features do not apply this reversal (deeper 7/7). Δ0.05 separates sampled bands, not a demonstrated sharp causal threshold; SGD/Adagrad extrapolation is unvalidated.
mechanism: With many distractor coordinates and only ~1024 rows, once the XOR interaction is learned (Δ≥0.05) further capacity of deep LN'd stacks is spent fitting distractor-dependent features and sharpening confidence near the axes, raising test CE; a shallow wide smooth net fits the 2-coordinate product with fewer composed nonlinearities. Predicts the reversal vanishes for ≤4 features (no distractors) or Δ<0.05 (boundary not yet learned) — both observed.

regime.note: Shared optimizer/lr/T; independent LN and residual-dependent depth preferences. No sharp boundary established.

phase: nf≥8: Δ≥0.05 smooth 15/16, more-LN 8/32, shallow vs ≥3 deeper 5/5; Δ<0.05 more-LN 33/41, shallow 4/14, smooth 3/8. nf<8: Δ≥0.05 more-LN 4/8, deeper 7/7 corpus + 2/2 lab; Δ<0.05 more-LN 8/11.

text: For depth≥3, ZERO-LN SGD MLPs versus a rival with Δ<0.1 and ≥3× smaller calibrated Δ, discount the nominal progress advantage; do not call them frozen or reject all SGD nets. Original within-set lab: larger-Δ zero-LN deep SGD won 21/60 (18 sets), median loss ratio ≈1.0; shallow zero-LN nets did much better (rectifier 80%, smooth 67%). With ≥1 LN, larger-Δ SGD won 493/563 (88%); do not apply the zero-LN penalty there. MSE zero-LN comparisons were only 37/70, so task-specific evidence matters. These are architecture/optimizer-confounded preferences, not a universal gradient bound. Examples: q_bfe225 and q_1469ce; calibration K1019.
mechanism: SGD's step is the raw gradient, so its true displacement scales with the backpropagated gradient magnitude. With PyTorch default init (weight std≈1/√(3·fan_in)) each unnormalized block shrinks activations and hence hidden-layer gradients geometrically, so |g|≈0.01 overestimates Δ for deep plain stacks. LayerNorm restores unit-RMS activations per block, and Adam-family divide by √v, so both are insensitive. Predicts: collapse grows with depth, absent with ≥1 LN or adaptive optimizers.

regime.note: SGD net vs rival with >=3x smaller calibrated Δ, rival Δ<0.1; lab within-set pairs

phase: SGD larger-Δ win rate: ≥1 LN 88% (493/563); 0 LN depth≤2 rect 80% (77/96), smooth 67% (60/90); 0 LN depth≥3 35% (21/60). Regression 0-LN 53% (37/70); classification 0-LN 69%.

text: Multivariate symbolic MSE, BOTH calibrated Δ<0.1 and Δ ratio 0.5-2: lean toward a non-residual MLP with exactly one extra LayerNorm over a residual rival; a skip is not one full LN point. Within-set lab: higher-LN plain wins 23/31 pairs (25 sets), median MSE ratio 0.906; equal optimizer/lr subset 4/6, ratio 0.913. Matched optimizer/lr training history: 41/53 pairs in 32 questions, including q_1f04dc (Adagrad 13/18). Do NOT extend above Δ=0.1 (lab 5/13, ratio 1.054) or to univariate (low-Δ 17/34, ratio 0.989). Width, depth, activation and optimizer knobs remain confounded; this is a preference, not a causal LN effect.

regime.note: Observational within-set comparisons; width/depth/activation/optimizer confounded; failed-seed sensitivity 22/30 vs23/31.
